citation: Droop, M., van Elsäcker, W., Voeten, M. J. M., & Verhoeven, L. (2016). Long-term effects of strategic reading instruction in the intermediate elementary grades. Journal of Research on Educational Effectiveness, 9(1), 77-102. https://doi.org/10.1080/19345747.2015.1065528
report_number: Journal of Research on Educational Effectiveness, 9(1), 77-102; DOI 10.1080/19345747.2015.1065528
design: Cluster (school-level) RCT; 40 schools / 62 classrooms randomized (22 schools/34 classes experimental, 18 schools/28 classes control); Grades 3-4 (two-year intervention in The Hague region, Netherlands); subject = reading comprehension; TPD = short teacher training to implement the Strategic Reading Instruction (SRI) program; control = regular school reading curriculum (business-as-usual). 1,469 students total (842 exp, 627 control).
problems: Legal green-OA copy: publisher Taylor & Francis PDF is hybrid-OA but blocks automated download (HTTP 403). PDF retrieved from the Radboud University institutional repository (Radboud Repository, hdl.handle.net/2066/155886), which hosts the FINAL PUBLISHED VERSION under Article 25fa of the Dutch Copyright Act (legal green OA). No piracy site used. | CLUSTER ADJUSTMENT NUANCE: randomization was at the SCHOOL level (40 schools), but the authors dropped the school level from the multilevel model (most schools had only 1-2 classes/grade) and used CLASSROOM (62) as the highest level. They explicitly state (p.90) that 'the clustering effect was not fully accounted for in the estimates of the standard errors ... possibly leading to a (slight) underestimation of these standard errors' (and a possible slight overestimation of z). So impact SEs are derived from a multilevel model that accounts for classroom (plus absorbed school) clustering but is not a full school-level cluster model; cluster_adjusted set true with this caveat. | Impact estimates and SEs are from Model 2 (intervention effect controlling for student-level background covariates; matches the authors' reported standardized d of 0.20 and 0.18). Model 4 (final parsimonious) gives near-identical coefficients (RCT b=0.885, PIRLS b=0.430). | Standardizing SD is sqrt(student-level intercept variance from Model 1), per the authors' own effect-size method (p.91): RCT SD=sqrt(20.368)=4.513; PIRLS SD=sqrt(5.784)=2.405. | NUMERIC SUBJECT n_t/n_c per outcome are the posttest (end Grade 4) Ns from Table 3 (RCT 517 control/674 exp; PIRLS mean 520 control/698 exp); model analytic Ns differ slightly (RCT N=1419 over 3 waves; PIRLS N=1433). | The study also reports a student-level 'Knowledge of Reading Strategies' outcome (end G4 d=0.67), but that is a metacognitive strategy-knowledge process measure tightly coupled to the intervention content, NOT a reading/vocabulary achievement test, so it is excluded from effect_sizes (noted here). Vocabulary and decoding were measured only as covariates, not as outcomes the intervention targeted.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Strategic Reading Instruction (SRI) teacher-training program vs business-as-usual reading curriculum
effect_sizes.test_name: Reading Comprehension Test (Aarnoutse & Schellings 2003; shortened 11-text/29-item version)
effect_sizes.timepoint: Post / end of Grade 4 (June 2011; end of 2-year treatment)
effect_sizes.g_method: d = b/SD = 0.914/4.513 = 0.203, where b = SRI x Change-end-Grade-4 coefficient from multilevel Model 2 (Table 5, p.94) and SD = sqrt(student-level intercept variance from Model 1) = sqrt(20.368) = 4.513 (authors' own standardizing SD, p.91). g = J*d, J = 1-3/(4*df-1) = 0.98745 with df = n_clusters-2 = 60 (model clustered at classroom level). g_se = J*(SE_b/SD) = 0.98745*(0.353/4.513). Matches authors' reported d=0.20.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 5 Model 2 p.94; descriptives Table 3 p.89-90; ES text p.95; ICC p.94
effect_sizes.notes: Headline reading-comprehension achievement outcome. Repeated-measures multilevel model on learning gains; positive intervention effect at end of Grade 4 (b=0.914, z=2.59, p=.010) but NOT at end of Grade 3 (interim wave: b=0.210, ns, d=0.04). Pretest favored control (exp group lower at baseline, b_pretest_diff=-1.011) but exp group caught up and overtook control after 2 years. Posttest raw means (Table 3) favor CONTROL (control 20.53 vs exp 19.87) because the model-based gain effect is adjusted for the lower exp pretest; the covariate-adjusted impact is positive and is the correct contrast (raw posttest g would be misleadingly negative due to baseline imbalance from differential school attrition). Standardizing SD from Model 1 student-level intercept variance. Pretest ICC=.19.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Strategic Reading Instruction (SRI) teacher-training program vs business-as-usual reading curriculum
effect_sizes.test_name: PIRLS Reading Literacy (one PIRLS-2006 booklet; mean of narrative + expository, max 33)
effect_sizes.timepoint: Post / end of Grade 4 (June 2011; end of 2-year treatment)
effect_sizes.g_method: d = b/SD = 0.428/2.405 = 0.178, where b = SRI x Change-end-Grade-4 coefficient from multilevel Model 2 (Table 6, p.95) and SD = sqrt(student-level intercept variance from Model 1) = sqrt(5.784) = 2.405 (authors' standardizing SD). g = J*d, J = 0.98745 (df = n_clusters-2 = 60). g_se = J*(SE_b/SD) = 0.98745*(0.205/2.405). Matches authors' reported d=0.18.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 6 Model 2/Model 4 p.95; descriptives Table 3 p.89-90; ES text p.96 (b=0.43, z=2.09, p<.05, d=0.18); ICC p.96
effect_sizes.notes: Second general reading-comprehension achievement outcome (independent standardized international assessment). Significant positive intervention effect at end of Grade 4 (b=0.428, z=2.088, p=.037) but NOT at end of Grade 3 (interim: b=-0.067, ns). As with the Reading Comprehension Test, raw posttest means slightly favor control due to baseline imbalance; covariate-adjusted model impact is positive (=correct contrast). NOTE: the end-of-Grade-4 PIRLS effect lost significance after additionally controlling for Raven nonverbal IQ (z=1.89, p=.059) or decoding (z=1.71, p=.086); the primary reported model (Model 4) effect is significant and is used here. PIRLS narrative/expository subtests analyzed separately in online Appendix D (narrative effect stronger); not extracted (subscales of this composite). Pretest ICC=.25.
